summary: The LocalizedText inspector: previews the key in every language and offers a picker of real keys.
overview: A localisation key is an opaque string, so the one question this inspector has to answer is "did I spell it right, and what does it actually say?" — without entering Play mode. Under the normal fields it lists the key's text in every language the project has, warns when a key resolves nowhere, and offers a Pick Key button listing the keys that genuinely exist.
useCases: Catching a typo now instead of finding #ui.strat_button# in a screenshot later.
Checking which languages have translated a line, while laying the screen out.
Finding the right key without opening the sheet.

walkthrough.name: Preview
walkthrough.what: One row per language: the text, or "— not translated —". Warns if the key is in no locale at all.

walkthrough.name: Pick Key...
walkthrough.what: A menu of every key that exists across the registry, with the current one ticked.

gotchas.title: It previews the registry the SCENE points at, not an arbitrary one
gotchas.body: It looks for a LocalizationManager in the open scene first, because that is the registry the label will actually read from at runtime. Only if there is none — a prefab, or a scene not set up yet — does it fall back to the first LocaleRegistry in the project, which may not be the one that ships.

gotchas.title: No preview means no registry, not a broken key
gotchas.body: With no LocaleRegistry anywhere it says so and stops, rather than reporting every key as missing.
